* WHERE...City of Hyder, Ketchikan Gateway Borough, and Prince of
Wales Island.

* WHEN...From 10 AM to 8 PM AKDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these unusually hot
temperatures for this region may experience heat related illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, and check up on elderly and vulnerable
relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear sunscreen and light loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles under any
circumstances as vehicle interiors can reach extreme temperatures in
as little as 10 minutes.

Close curtains during the daytime to reduce sun insulation into the
home and open windows at night to allow the home to cool off. Utilize
fans or community buildings with air conditioning.

concentrations that pose a health risk. Adverse health effects

for children, older adults, as well as persons with respiratory
problems. A decrease in physical activity is recommended.

The use of gasoline-powered equipment should be reduced or done late
in the day.

site at www.azdeq.gov/forecast/phoenix or call 602-771-2300.

northeast, including the communities of Volcano and Mountain View.

lightweight pumice may fall downwind of the eruption. These small

level impacts for most people.

sensitivities. Wear a mask, gloves, eye protection, and long
clothing when clearing ashfall. Close windows and doors. Cover and
disconnect water catchment systems to protect your water supply.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued May 31 at 11:49AM AKDT until June 3 at 10:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...The following areas, Kodiak Island. This includes the
cities of Kodiak City, Port Lions, Ouzinkie, Old Harbor.

* WHEN...From Monday morning through Wednesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff from heavy rain may result in flooding
of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone
locations, including Bells Flats. Expected heavy rain may saturate
soils resulting in isolated landslides in areas of steep terrain.
Strong east to northeast winds gusting to near 60 mph at times may
also result in downed trees due to saturated soils.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An unseasonably strong North Pacific low south of Kodiak
Island is expected to bring an atmospheric river of moisture
across Kodiak Island Monday morning through Tuesday night. 2
to 4 inches of rain is possible along the eastern coast of
the island with 3 to 6 inches of rain possible for the higher
terrain. 1 inch or less of rain is possible across the
western coast of the island. The heaviest rain is expected to
fall between noon Monday and noon Tuesday, with the bulk of
the expected storm total rainfall falling during this time.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

- All residents on or near mountain slopes should be prepared for
possible landslides.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.
